data.content_ref: inline:Artifact 18174034ea0c contradicts artifact 2f8f85328fae on the locus of the replay-correctness obligation: 18174034ea0c places the requirement on the writer (idempotency ensures the log is identical regardless of retry count, so deterministic replay sees one canonical stream), while 2f8f85328fae relocates it entirely to the consumer's fold operation (commutativity of the fold tolerates duplicates, so the writer need only append). The contradiction is substantive because the two views prescribe incompatible system designs—writer-side deduplication keys versus consumer-side duplicate suppression—and disagree on whether a safe-but-non-idempotent writer is acceptable for deterministic replay. Refuted if the fold's commutativity is merely a structural relocation of writer idempotency, such that both prescriptions collapse to the same invariant (no duplicate effects survive to final state), making the two views compatible rather than contradictory. This abstention from contradiction would be forced when 2f8f85328fae's own counterconditions hold: if the fold is not commutative or events lack deduplication metadata, then writer idempotency becomes necessary after all, vindicating 18174034ea0c and confirming the contradiction rather than dissolving it.
